articles.title: Maharashtra sets up drought mitigation panel, approves ₹291.91 crore relief for flood-hit farmers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Maharashtra government on Monday (November 1, 2026) announced measures to address drought and flood-related agricultural distress across the State, constituting a high-level committee headed by the Chief Minister to oversee soil and water conservation projects in drought-affected areas and approving ₹291.91 crore in financial assistance for farmers affected by heavy rainfall and flooding between June and August 2026.

Soil and Water Conservation Minister Sanjay Rathod said the committee would monitor conservation projects undertaken through non-governmental organisations, including Paani Foundation and Chandra Foundation, as part of the state’s drought mitigation efforts. The government has also decided to revive Paani Foundation’s Water Cup competition to encourage community participation in water conservation.
The measures follow deficient rainfall in parts of Maharashtra during 2026, prompting the government to declare drought in talukas identified under the Kharif season’s Trigger-1 assessment.

According to a government resolution issued on November 2, all Deputy Chief Ministers will serve as co-chairpersons of the high-level committee, which will include ministers from departments such as agriculture, water resources, rural development and employment guarantee.

A separate executive committee, chaired by the Principal Secretary of the Water Resources Department, will coordinate implementation and meet at least once a month. Progress will be monitored using geographical information systems (GIS), satellite imagery, mobile-based monitoring systems and online dashboards.

Meanwhile, Relief and Rehabilitation Minister Makarand Jadhav Patil announced that the government had sanctioned ₹262.70 crore for crop damage affecting 3,09,289 farmers across six revenue divisions, including Pune, Nagpur, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Amravati, Konkan and Nashik.

An additional ₹29.21 crore has been approved for damage to agricultural land covering 7,675.40 hectares belonging to 34,984 farmers. The assistance will cover eligible restoration work, including the removal of sand, silt and salt deposits caused by flooding.

Crop damage compensation will be transferred directly to eligible farmers’ bank accounts, while small and marginal landowners will receive assistance for damaged agricultural land up to a maximum of two hectares, in accordance with prescribed norms.
The government has also directed district collectors to ensure that banks do not divert disaster relief payments towards loan repayments or other recoveries.

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi acting as a ‘toolkit’ for foreign forces says Nitin Nabin
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) president Nitin Nabin on Monday (November 2, 2026) accused Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi of leading those trying to create “anarchy” in the country and acting as a “toolkit” for foreign forces attempting to destabilise India.

A day after the Opposition INDIA bloc, led by Mr. Gandhi’s Congress party, held a gathering at Delhi’s Ramlila Grounds over allegations of ‘vote theft’ and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), Mr. Nabin held a procession in Kolkata titled ‘Save Democracy, End Anarchy’. The march which was joined by thousands of supporters was a show of strength for the saffron party.

“Rahul Gandhi is acting as a toolkit of those forces which engineered the unrest in Nepal and other neighbouring countries. If you think you will destabilise India, if you think you will work as a toolkit for those who are destabilising Europe, those who are destabilising Bangladesh or Nepal, then know that Indian democracy is very strong ,” Mr. Nabin alleged.

The march, organised under the banner ‘Save Democracy, End Anarchy’, began at College Street and proceeded towards Dharmatala in central Kolkata, with hundreds of BJP supporters including Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and State BJP president Samik Bhattacharya joining the procession.

Targeting the Congress for “trying to spread anarchy in the entire country by targeting constitutional institutions of the country” Mr. Nabin said that if the Congress had fought for the issues of the people, the people would not have rejected the party.
“They say the democracy and Constitution are under threat whenever they lose elections, but when they win elections conducted by the same Election Commission of India,” Mr. Nabin added.
He cited the victory of Congress party in Keralam Assembly elections and asked, “Had SIR been the issue, how did Congress win in Keralam?”

The BJP leader said that all the anarchy had been eradicated from West Bengal on May 4, when the BJP came to power, defeating Mamata Banerjee. Raising questions about the new bonhomie between the Congress and Mamata Banerjee, Mr. Nabin said that during the Assembly elections, Rahul Gandhi came here and spoke against corruption and misrule of the Mamata Banerjee regime and now both are sharing the stage.
Mr. Nabin said that the Congress and its allies are not interested in the welfare of 140 crore people in the county and in interested in the well-being of only three crore infiltrators.
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, who also spoke at the culmination of the rally, said that for the BJP the SIR stood for ‘Remove Infiltrators, Save India’.

“Those who have united to save themselves from corruption, imprisonment and to protect their families and bring back the politics of appeasement should remember that the Bharatiya Janata Party was elected in West Bengal in 2026 with 2.92 crore votes. For us, SIR means ‘Remove Infiltrators, Save India’. That is why they are trying to create anarchy in the state,”Mr. Adhikari said.
The first BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal warned Opposition parties that they would face a decisive political response in the forthcoming Kolkata and Howrah municipal corporation elections.

articles.title: Congress seeks JPC probe into IDBI Bank sale, alleges valuation irregularities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Congress on Monday (November 2, 2026) demanded an immediate halt to the proposed sale of IDBI Bank to Canada’s Fairfax Financial Holdings and a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) probe into the transaction, alleging that the government had manipulated the bank’s valuation.
The party alleged that the foreign buyer would use the bank’s own funds to finance the acquisition.

Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh separately described the transaction as a “major scam” by the Narendra Modi government and demanded that both valuation reports be made public.
Addressing a press conference, senior Congress leader Shaktisinh Gohil alleged that the disinvestment process was riddled with irregularities and lacked transparency.

Citing a conversation between an analyst and Fairfax Chairman Prem Watsa and President Peter Clarke, Mr. Gohil claimed that the company had indicated that the payment would be made in instalments, with the initial investment followed by the use of IDBI Bank’s resources to meet the remaining acquisition cost.
“Prem Watsa is a very close to Modi ji and had showered praise on him during the 2017 Vibrant Gujarat Summit,” the Congress leader said.

Mr. Gohil questioned the rationale of selling a profitable Indian bank to a foreign company using its own funds. He said IDBI Bank had earned a cumulative profit of ₹30,105 crore between 2021 and 2026 and had non-performing assets of only about 2%.
Its profit per employee stood at ₹49.8 lakh, making it one of the leading banks on this measure, he said. “Why is a bank that is delivering such high profits being sold?” he asked.

The Congress leader also questioned the revision of the bank’s valuation from ₹94.42 to ₹75 a share after the bids had been opened. He said the government had initially fixed the valuation at ₹94.42 a share before inviting bids, but subsequently revised it downwards.

articles.title: Capex push to continue, but fiscal prudence non-negotiable: FM
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Union Finance and Corporate Affairs Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Monday reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to sustaining capital expenditure (capex) to support economic growth, while stressing that fiscal prudence would remain non-negotiable.

“Capex is a very important component of our growth strategy. Because till such time the private sector will be able to expand capacity or make capital investment, it is important for the Government to push through with capital investment,” she said at an event organised by HSBC India in Mumbai.
Pointing to the returns from public investment over the past four to five years, she said the multiplier effects had strengthened the Government’s confidence in continuing the spending push.

“We find that in the last 4 to 5 years, we have got very good success. The multipliers actually work and it gives us confidence that the Government is not going to sit back and watch whether growth is growing without doing much,” she said.

The Government would be willing to extend capex support to ensure that the growth momentum was not disrupted. “We will continue doing that because India’s growth momentum should not be lost at all,” she said.
However, Ms. Sitharaman made it clear that higher public spending would have to be balanced against fiscal constraints.
“We need to be fiscally prudent,” she said, adding that while some advocated spending without worrying about sovereign credit ratings, responsible expenditure was essential.
“I agree we need to spend but it has to be done responsibly and fiscal prudence will be our top priority,” she emphasised.
“We have to be prudent and we have to be creative based on which we can encourage growth and stability,” she added.
The Finance Minister also called for greater confidence in India’s economic prospects, urging businesses and experts to move beyond pessimism and sector-specific concerns.

“India must to talk with optimism and there needs to be reduction in cynicism,” she said, questioning why experts who considered their own sectors healthy remained apprehensive about the broader economy.
“If your sector doing fine, others sectors in India must be similarly fine. So can the narrate and language change?” she asked.

A bank or finance firm funds the purchase and charges interest. The shop agrees to bear interest but it will recover it in one of two ways. Either the price quoted to you is higher, or you lose the discount a cash buyer would have got Take the same phone. A cash buyer gets it for ₹57,000. The EMI buyer pays ₹60,000. The ₹3,000 gap is the interest.

The Kolkata-headquartered miner said that its supplies to the power sector also increased 19% to touch 57.1 MT. articles.title: GST mop-up surges 23% to second-highest level of ₹2.31 lakh crore in October on festive demand boost
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: GST collections jumped 23% year-on-year to the second-highest level of over ₹2.31 lakh crore in October as festive buying boosted domestic demand, according to government data released on Sunday (November 1, , 2026).
October is the second consecutive month when monthly gross Goods and Services Tax (GST) crossed ₹2 lakh crore, and second only to the record about ₹2.43 lakh crore mop-up in April.
Also, the 22.9% year-on-year growth clocked during the month is the fastest recorded pace of gross mop-up in the current fiscal year.
Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16% to over ₹1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42% to ₹72,246 crore.
The ₹2.31 lakh crore collection includes Central GST mop-up of 42,935 crore, State GST of ₹51,340 crore and Integrated GST of over ₹1.37 lakh crore, data showed.
Goods and Services Tax (GST) refunds increased 6.5% year-on-year to ₹27,934 crore in October.
After adjusting for refunds, net GST collections rose 26% to over ₹2.03 lakh crore in October.
In April-October, gross GST collection grew 13.2% to over ₹14.77 lakh crore. Net collections rose 13% to over ₹12.69 lakh crore.

Grant Thornton Bharat, Partner and Tax Controversy Management Leader, Manoj Mishra, said October collections capture the festive-season demand cycle, which typically brings higher consumer spending, retail activity and movement of goods across sectors.
The performance across key states, including Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, also points to continued strength in GST collections across major economic centres.

“The focus now should be on sustaining domestic revenue growth and ensuring that the benefits of GST 2.0 translate into stronger compliance, smoother input tax credit flows and faster refunds for businesses,” Mr. Mishra said.

EY India Tax Partner, Saurabh Agarwal, said the GST collections for October 2026 reflect the continued resilience of the Indian economy, despite persistent global headwinds. The steady month-on-month rise in revenue indicates strong underlying consumption and improving compliance.

articles.title: India’s coal imports decline 5.83% in August
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India’s overall import of coal fell 5.83% in August from the same period last year on the back of increased domestic production of the fossil fuel compound and reduced their shipments from overseas, according to government data.
The country imported 104.57 million tonnes (MT) of coal in August, compared to 111.05 MT in the same period last year.
Imports by domestic coal-based (DCB) power plants, that require the carbon-based compound for blending purposes, slumped 35.23% to 3 MT.
However, imports of thermal power plants that run solely on imported coal registered an uptick of about 1% at 18.31 MT.
Overall, coal imports by the power sector slumped about 6.4%.
The share of imported coal in India’s overall consumption basket declined to 19.3% in August this year compared to 21.2% in the same month last year.
Other than the power sector, coking coal, which serves as an important input for the steel industry, also declined about 4.2% during the reported period to 27.3 MT.
India depends on imports to meet 95% of its coking coal requirements. Import requirements are therefore subject to the demand of the steel sector.

Reflecting on the import dynamics, the Union Coal Ministry held, “The decline in overall coal imports, particularly imports for blending at domestic coal-based power plants, underscores the importance of strengthening domestic production, transportation and supply-chain infrastructure,” adding that imports by imported coal-based power plants and the steel sector reflect their specific fuel and raw material requirements.

articles.title: Netanyahu pressing Trump to attack Iran after midterms, says officials
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for another wave of strikes on Iran after Tuesday's (November 3, 2026) midterm elections in the United States, according to two regional officials and a third person familiar with the matter.

A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Mr. Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week's elections. U.S. President Donald Trump has alternated between threatening major strikes while pushing for a deal with Iran.

The two officials said diplomatic efforts have made progress, with Qatari mediators holding two rounds of talks last week with Iranian officials. The two officials said the mediators are trying to advance a framework for Iran to cease its attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in return for the U.S. lifting its blockade on Iran's ports.

They said more talks are planned for this week. The two officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were discussing classified briefings they had received from American, and in one case Israeli, officials.

One official said Mr. Netanyahu was working with senior officials in the U.S. administration to persuade Mr. Trump to launch a quick but extensive air campaign and that the president does not appear to have made a decision.
Mr. Netanyahu pressed for strikes during a call over the weekend with Mr. Trump, who would not commit to taking military action, according to a person who was briefed on it.

Other U.S. allies in West Asia are warning against more strikes, saying it would destabilise the region and could lead Iran-allied Houthi rebels in Yemen to step up their attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping, a third regional official said. Iran-backed militias in Iraq could also get involved.
That official, and the person familiar with the Netanyahu-Trump call, were not authorised to speak publicly and spoke on condition of anonymity.

The Israeli government did not immediately comment. The White House did not directly respond to questions about Mr. Netanyahu and Mr. Trump's discussion of potential new strikes during the weekend call.

Mr. Trump told reporters on Sunday (November 1, 2026) that he and Mr. Netanyahu had a “very good” call the day before. He said they discussed Iran but gave no details. Mr. Netanyahu had pushed for renewed strikes even before the Israeli election as he sought to highlight his security credentials to a public deeply scarred by Hamas' October 7, 2023, attack.

Asked at a news conference on Saturday (October 31, 2026) about the possibility of new U.S. strikes on Iran and Iranian retaliation, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio would not say what would happen next but reiterated that the Trump administration prefers a diplomatic solution and that talks were ongoing.
“He hasn't made a decision,” Mr. Rubio said, referring to Mr. Trump.

articles.title: An anti-climactic outcome in the Knesset elections
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: For the Israeli Knesset election hyped as “consequential” and a “day of reckoning for the October 7 Hamas attack”, the verdict points to new trends and the normalisation of trenchant nationalism. The inconclusive outcome risks disappointing most stakeholders. Israel, being at the epicentre of the ongoing regional tumult, needs a real-time analysis.

Israel’s total electorate is 7.3 million. Yet it has 38 officially recognised political parties vying for 120 Knesset seats, of which only 11 parties are likely to cross the 3.25% voting threshold needed to enter the legislature. The elections are on a proportional representation basis. The parties are currently arrayed in three coalitions: the ruling extreme right, the centrist bloc and the Israeli-Arab bloc which got 53, 48 and 19 seats, respectively. The last group representing a 21% minority is largely untouchable for mainstream Jewish parties. The electorate is also split along ethnic and origin-based lines into occidental, oriental and orthodox cohorts. Since the last elections in 2022, nearly half a million new voters have come of age. The voter turnout jumped by nearly a tenth to 77.7% — a sign of sharp political engagement.

articles.title: Many U.K. social care migrant workers to get PR in five years under softer immigration overhaul
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Foreign social and home care workers, who arrived in the U.K. before May 2025, will be able to normally settle (become permanent residents) in five years, rather than in 15 years, as was first proposed in the British government’s ‘earned settlement’ scheme announced in November 2025.

Those earning more than £50,271 per annum, doctors, nurses and teachers will be able to settle in five years, while those earning more than £1,25,140 per annum could settle in three years, as was proposed in the November 2025 draft rules.

The news of softer final rules for care workers is likely to impact thousands of Indians who came in on the Health and Care Worker visa scheme, which began in October 2020 and ran until July 2025. The scheme is associated with reports of Indian care workers – including many from Kerala – being subject to abuse, including unpaid wages, illegal recruitment fees, threats and other forms of exploitation at the hands of employers.

Under the scheme, finalised on Monday (November 2, 2026), social care workers earning at least £25,000 per year, who arrived in the U.K. before May 2025, would be eligible for ‘indefinite leave to remain’ (ILR) after five years. Those who have fallen afoul of the initial visa conditions would be given “a second chance”, U.K. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said, with a fresh five-year qualifying period.

“The government has already stripped around 1,800 exploitative employers of their licenses,” Ms. Mahmood said on Monday (November 2, 2026), adding that the government would help workers find positions with legitimate care providers.

The softening of the conditions for residency in the final version of the earned settlement rules, announced by Ms. Mahmood, was a response to pressure from the left flank of the Labour Party and health unions, as well as a response to a public consultation on the draft policy, conducted earlier this year. The U.K. government said that over 2,02,000 responses were received, most (73%) of whom were visa holders.

The government had originally announced the draft earned settlement scheme under pressure from the parties on the right, especially Reform U.K., which, at the time, was surging in popularity. The basis of the overhaul was to increase the default qualifying period for settlement from five to ten years, with various factors either adding to or lowering the default qualifying duration of time.

The government, headed at the time by Prime Minister Keir Starmer, had argued the immigration overhaul was necessary to counter the surge in migration (sometimes called the ‘Boriswave’) in the social care and student categories that happened after Covid, during the administration of Boris Johnson, a Conservative.

Net migration hit a record of 9,44,000 in the year ending March 2023. However, following a tightening in policy started by the Rishi Sunak government and continued by Mr. Starmer’s Labour government, the net figure as of December 2025 dropped to 1,71,000.

“10 billion pounds. That is the cost of today’s U-turn,” shadow (i.e., opposition) Home Secretary Chris Philp said in the House of Commons on Monday (November 2, 2026), using Ms. Mahmood’s own cost estimate against her. He alleged that Ms. Mahmood was not in control of the government’s immigration policy and that Housing Secretary Angela Rayner, who is a prominent figure on Labour’s left, was in charge.

Other low-income workers could now obtain ILR in 10 years rather than the 15 years proposed under the draft scheme announced last year. Those with ILR have the right to live and work in the U.K. permanently and to potentially apply for benefits (public assistance).

The qualifying period for refugees and those arriving in the U.K. via illegal routes, would range from five to 30 years depending on whether they were studying, working, and how they arrived in the county.

articles.title: In first high-level visit after new government’s arrival, Foreign Secretary Misri to visit Nepal on November 4-5
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri will pay a two-day visit to Kathmandu on November 4 and 5, the Ministry of External Affairs announced on Monday (November 2, 2026). This will be the first visit by Mr. Misri to Nepal since Prime Minister Balendra Shah took charge in March this year following the election that was conducted under an interim government. A visit to India by Mr. Shah is understandably part of the agenda that will be discussed when Mr. Misri meets officials in Kathmandu.

“Foreign Secretary’s upcoming visit continues the tradition of regular high-level exchanges between the two countries and will help further enhance the comprehensive bilateral partnership,” said the Ministry in an announcement. The visit by Mr. Misri to Kathmandu will be keenly watched as it comes amid a slew of reforms that Nepal’s post-Gen-Z uprising government is in the process of rolling out.

Apart from Mr. Shah’s visit to India, Mr. Misri’s conversations in Kathmandu are likely to feature the appointment of a new Ambassador of Nepal to New Delhi. Nepali Embassy has been without an Ambassador for several months since the previous Ambassador, Shankar Prasad Sharma, returned home. Nepali diplomatic sources told The Hindu earlier that Kathmandu was waiting for the agrément (diplomatic approval) for new envoy Nischal Nath Pandey to take charge in the embassy here. India’s continued assistance to the disaster in Bhote Koshi river is also expected to be on the agenda.

Even as Mr. Misri's visit was being announced by the Ministry, a welfare association of former Indian Army soldiers took out a protest in Kathmandu on Monday (November 2) demanding that Gurkha recruitment into the Indian Army be resumed. Recruitment of Gurkha soldiers remains suspended since the Agnipath scheme was introduced by the Government of India.

The Hindu had earlier reported that Mr. Misri was expected to visit Nepal in May, but the visit was postponed ostensibly because Mr. Shah had prioritised domestic challenges. The India visit by Mr. Shah, if it materialises, will be the first bilateral visit abroad by the leader who came into prominence during the September 2025 Gen-Z uprising that overthrew the government of Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli. Mr. Misri had visited Kathmandu previously for two days in August 2025 and had met Mr. Oli.

In the past few months, India has hosted Nepal’s Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal, Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, and Home Minister Sudan Gurung, who visited Delhi to participate in the first BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) meet held on October 13, 2026. India has also hosted the head of the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) Rabi Lamichhane in the first week of June when he met Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr. Lamichhane paid a personal visit to India last week to pray at the pilgrimage centres in Kainchi Dham in Uttarakhand and the Kamakhya temple in Guwahati.

Mr. Lamichhane had described this visit as “personal and not political”. “There are no political meetings planned. Since this is a personal visit, I urge people not to read politics into it,” said Mr. Lamichhane before starting the visit.

articles.title: Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if U.S. agrees to demands
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Iran on Monday (November 2, 2026) said it was ready to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington agrees to conditions, as U.S. President Donald Trump issued his latest war threat at a rally for midterm elections.
A senior Iranian official said the offer to open the vital energy corridor, which follows intense efforts by mediators to stop a return to war, showed "good faith".

Tehran has blockaded Hormuz since the war started in February, sending energy prices soaring and posing an electoral challenge for Trump. The narrow gateway to the energy-rich Gulf normally carries one-fifth of global oil consumption.
"The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran's good-faith approach," Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told reporters at a briefing.
"We have stated that, if Iran's demands are met, it would be possible to restore security to the Strait of Hormuz and resume the negotiating process within a short period."

In September, Iran proposed a seven-day plan to reopen Hormuz if the U.S. agreed to demands including ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending its counter-blockade of Iranian ports.
Mr. Baqaei said messages were being exchanged with the United States via mediators, adding that "everything depends" on the U.S. side accepting the Iranian demands.
During final rallies for the U.S. midterms on Tuesday (November 3), where diesel prices and consumer inflation are a key issue, Trump struck a belligerent tone, warning Iran to expect "the hammer".

"The only reason why I'm not finished with Iran is I want to be nice. I want to try and save all those lives if I can... But at some point we're going to have to give them the hammer," he told voters in Iowa.
Officials from Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Turkey have held talks with Iran in recent days, while U.S. Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Tehran.
Oman's ruler Sultan Haitham bin Tariq discussed the war with Chinese President Xi Jinping during a visit to Beijing on Monday (November 2), an Omani foreign ministry statement said.

"The two sides called for resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means, urging the United States and Iran to pursue a peaceful path, achieve a ceasefire (and) prevent war entirely," it said, calling for "dialogue and negotiations as soon as possible".

articles.title: U.K. warns EU against keeping Britain out of ‘Made in Europe’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: U.K. Defence Minister Wes Streeting on Monday (November 1, 2026) warned the EU against keeping Britain out of its "Made in Europe" industrial push, weeks before a key EU-U.K. summit.

The European Union wants to boost domestic sectors like cars and defence by forcing companies to buy European if they want public money, but the efforts have raised concerns in London about the U.K.'s potential exclusion.

"We need to be careful" to avoid that the Made in Europe push "doesn't spread into self-defeating protectionism", Streeting said alongside top EU diplomat Kaja Kallas ahead of their talks in Brussels.
The British Minister will also meet EU Defence Chief Andrius Kubilius.
Monday's (November 2) talks come just over two weeks before EU chiefs and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham will meet for a summit in Brussels on November 20.
Mr. Burnham has said the long-awaited meeting would be a chance to start a "serious dialogue" about long-term relations between the U.K. and the bloc, a decade after the Brexit vote to leave.
One of the major issues on the table this month will be "Made in Europe" even though it is not officially on the summit's agenda.

As the EU's push to cut dependence on non-EU companies widens to include artificial intelligence development and cloud computing, the U.K. fears new digital rules being prepared will also exclude British companies.
London and Brussels hope to clinch deals on food and drink trade, youth mobility and avoiding EU carbon emissions taxes during the November 20 talks.
The EU hopes to make progress especially on cutting the fees EU students have to pay to attend British universities.
The bloc's capitals will discuss the draft of a joint EU-U.K. summit statement during a meeting of ambassadors Wednesday in Brussels.
Streeting will also meet German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius later on Monday (November 2) in Berlin.

articles.title: How AI training models could compromise privacy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The right to privacy is a constitutional right upheld by the Supreme Court in 2017. However, the legal instruments currently in place to safeguard this right seem inadequate, especially considering the technological revolution led by Artificial Intelligence (AI) around the world. While AI regulation is one of the most commonly discussed issues within governments today, the recommendations have been broad, vague and have only led to further questions. AI has immense potential to boost productivity and have positive effects on people’s lives; any indiscriminate regulatory or policy measure risks inhibiting innovation and economic growth. However, there are lower hanging fruits; specific gaps that can be filled to better safeguard people’s constitutional rights without permanently losing out in the AI race.

The Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act was passed in 2023, with the DPDP Rules being notified in November 2025. The implementation is phased with some provisions on consent and safety becoming effective only in 2027. Prior to the DPDP Act, the primary legal instrument to regulate the use and management of personal data was the Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000. Together the IT Act, 2000 and its 2011 Rules broadly regulated the export of “sensitive personal data” on the condition that the recipient ensured a level of data protection required under Indian law, and that the transfer was either necessary to perform a lawful contract or had been consented to by the data provider. An assertion and claim were sufficient to record adequacy. The criminal penalty for unauthorised disclosure was capped at three years’ imprisonment or a fine of ₹5 lakh. These penalties only applied to disclosure of sensitive personal data that were listed in the Rules such as financial data, medical or health details, sexual orientation, biometric information etc. The Rules did not apply to personal data such as names, addresses, phone numbers, caste, religion, political affiliations, browsing history, social media activity, online or offline behavioural patterns, institutional affiliations etc.

articles.title: Ebola reminder of urgent need to finish pandemic treaty: WHO chief
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Deadly outbreaks like the Ebola epidemic raging in the Democratic Republic of Congo show the urgent need to complete an international pandemic treaty, the World Health Organization chief said Monday.
Wealthy countries and developing nations remain at loggerheads over how an agreement, adopted last year as a framework to handle future Covid-like pandemics, will work in practice.
As the ninth meeting towards finalising the deal opened in Geneva Monday, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called on countries to "finish the job".
Pointing to several recent deadly disease outbreaks, he stressed that completing a pandemic treaty was "about protecting people".
"A pathogen threat anywhere can become a threat everywhere, to people of every country," he said, according to a written version of his statement.
"The outbreak of hantavirus earlier this year, and the ongoing Ebola epidemic in DRC remind us of this threat."

He was referring to the hantavirus outbreak that killed three people on a cruise ship in April and the latest Ebola outbreak, declared in May, which has killed nearly 5,000 people out of more than 10,000 infected mostly in the DRC.
It was vital, Tedros said, that the world learn the overarching lesson of the Covid-19 pandemic: "no country can protect itself from pandemics by acting alone".
When countries agreed in May 2025 to a Pandemic Agreement, they left out the tricky issue of how the key mechanism would operate to get the deal over the line.

The agreement's Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) system covers how to share access to pathogens with pandemic potential, as well as benefits derived from them such as vaccines, tests and treatments.
"PABS is the last remaining piece of our puzzle," Tedros said.
During the Covid pandemic, he highlighted that "the world developed vaccines in record time, but too many countries were left waiting while others secured far more than they needed".

articles.title: Vietnam scraps child organ donors proposal after backlash
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Vietnam withdrew on Monday a proposal allowing children aged 15 to 17 to donate their organs after death following public criticism in a country where deceased donor transplants remain limited.
The Southeast Asian country began kidney transplants in 1992 and performs the most annual transplants in the region, according to state media.
However, the vast majority of transplants in Vietnam rely on living donors. Transplants in many other nations mostly use organs from deceased donors, expanding their donor pool.
Officials in Vietnam say they are seeking to update a 2006 law on organ and tissue donation, aiming to increase life-saving transplants while safeguarding donors.

A draft submitted to the National Assembly last month proposed allowing 15- to 17-year-olds to donate their tissues, organs or bodies after death, provided the child's parent or legal representative consented.

But, after online backlash, officials removed the under-18 donor provision from a revised draft dated Sunday, with the government saying it had accepted recommendations from lawmakers that only legal adults should be permitted to donate their organs.
Dissent is heavily restricted in communist Vietnam, but opposition centred on whether parental consent could adequately protect child donors from pressure or exploitation.
Criticism also focused on a survey of schoolchildren as young as seven conducted in October to gather feedback on the draft law.
The poll prompted questions about whether minors could understand complex medical, legal and ethical issues, state outlet Tuoi Tre News said.
It said "the provision allowing minors to register as posthumous organ donors prompted considerable controversy and differing opinions among the public".
"Taking these concerns into account, the government has revised the draft," stipulating that only people aged 18 or older may donate their organs, Tuoi Tre said.
National Assembly deputy Pham Khanh Phong Lan urged lawmakers last month to oppose allowing child organ donors, saying: "You cannot sacrifice one child to save another."

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Women recruited from economically weaker sections were being offered ₹20,000 to ₹30,000 for an egg donation cycle, while those operating the alleged racket made an average of about ₹3 lakh from each cycle.
Malkajgiri police widened their investigation into the exploitation of women, falsification of records and the role of IVF and fertility establishments.

The 43 women rescued during simultaneous raids in Hyderabad have undergone medical examinations, including blood-group and fitness tests. Police are now verifying their medical histories with IVF centres to establish their treatment records.

The investigation has raised concerns over how the women were recruited and whether they gave informed consent for the procedures. Police said women from economically weaker sections were targeted and that, in some cases, intermediaries allegedly even completed their signatures on documents. Investigators are examining possible falsification of records and whether the women fully understood the procedures they were being recruited for.
Police are tracing the payments and commissions involving organisers, recruiters and intermediaries who connected the women with fertility-related establishments.

The investigation is now expanding to medical establishments. Police are preparing to serve notices to the District Medical and Health Officer (DMHO) and conduct searches at ART and fertility centres. Some hospitals have also approached police and informed them that employees found to have been involved had been removed.

Investigators are examining how women from West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and other states were recruited, transported and accommodated in Hyderabad before being referred for egg retrieval procedures. Their medical records, consent documents and the procedures they underwent are also being scrutinised.
All eight accused arrested in connection with the Hyderabad cases have been remanded to judicial custody. Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: What a new global study on pain reveals about women’s experiences
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Women are more likely than men to report pain across every one of the 11 anatomical sites examined in a global study involving more than 6.1 million people across 118 countries. The study found that differences were particularly pronounced for facial pain, headaches and abdominal pain.

Published in Nature Medicine , the study found that women had 83% higher relative prevalence of facial pain, 74% higher prevalence of headaches and 60% higher prevalence of stomach or abdominal pain than men. Women were also more likely to report high-intensity and widespread pain, highlighting a disparity that extends beyond the occurrence of pain to its severity and distribution.

fullParagraphs: The gathering of hundreds of thousands of people at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan, organised by the Congress-led INDIA bloc parties, was a milestone in the battle for the restoration of the integrity of India’s election process. As more and more skeletons tumble out the of the closet of the Election Commission of India (ECI), its chief Gyanesh Kumar has chosen silence while the ruling BJP has rushed to shield him from criticism. The united outcry of protest by the Opposition, led by the Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi , is a strong signal of public opinion for the ruling party and India’s institutions, including the ECI, that appear complicit in a scheme that threatens the foundations of Indian democracy. What remains unexplained by the ECI and Mr. Kumar are malpractices in the Special Intensive Revision that could have the effect of subverting the popular will. Protestors on Sunday had arrived from all parts of India, and included people directly affected by the SIR across the country.

The protest reinforced Mr. Gandhi’s central role as the key challenger of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr. Gandhi, for all his faults, has been an uncompromising champion of constitutional values and pluralism in India. The BJP caricatured him, and even non-BJP voices had bought into the idea of Mr. Gandhi being a privileged dynast out of touch with the commoner. While his ancestry is a matter of fact, so is his tenacity. All Opposition parties mobilised for the protest, but the centrality of the Congress party was unmistakable. Mr. Gandhi has a special focus on subaltern classes to be included in positions of responsibility in the party. The Sunday protest was clearly the largest show of strength in recent memory. The manner in which the Congress coordinated with the wide spectrum of the Opposition, often involving rivals in States, also indicates a clear sense of purpose and pragmatism. The call for the restoration of institutional integrity is the need of the hour; but Mr. Gandhi must be careful not to misstate the nature of the crisis. In his well-reasoned call for accountability of the ECI, Mr. Gandhi ended up questioning the legitimacy of the previous election without providing any substantive basis for his allegations. He must remember that his emergence as the voice of the Opposition places on him the responsibility of being measured in his speeches and his steps.
Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls / Election Commission of India / demonstration / Rahul Gandhi

articles.title: Cascading effect: On dams and land rights
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The bureaucratic impetus for the 11.2-GW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh purportedly comes from China’s aggressive development of a 60-GW mega-dam in Tibet , stoking anxieties among Indian authorities over ‘weaponised’ transboundary waters. Beijing may be able to divert flows in the Yarlung Tsangpo river, which becomes the Brahmaputra in India, to cause drought downstream or release water en masse to trigger catastrophic floods in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. New Delhi thus imagines SUMP as a strategic buffer, but in so doing faces a dilemma it should not attempt to resolve with force. Its extant top-down approach, exemplified by deploying security forces to guard survey teams and imposing the State Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act against activists, only validates fears among locals that the state will grab their land. The region also hosts sustained protests against the Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project , expanding the indictment to Arunachal Pradesh’s model of hydroelectric power development. The eastern Himalayas are among the most tectonically active and erosion-prone landscapes in the world. The mega-dam in Tibet will comprise five cascading power stations over the river’s roughly 2,000-metre fall over 50 km. Beijing has maintained the dam will not harm countries downstream but has declined to share crucial engineering details. This is why diplomacy will be an essential part of operating SUMP, in addition to Beijing’s disputed claims on Arunachal Pradesh.

The Brahmaputra basin in Assam and Bangladesh receives most of its water from monsoon rains and tributaries downstream of the Tibetan Plateau, so China cannot straightforwardly control the river’s total flow through India. Yet since Chinese interventions would have greater consequences closer to the border, SUMP will need information about both the mega-dam’s operations and downstream inflows to plan its own operations, and Beijing has declined to share the former. SUMP thus faces many uncertainties at the outset. Despite India repeatedly raising the issue with China at the highest levels, headway has been limited to Beijing agreeing to share hydrological data on humanitarian grounds during emergencies. Planners have contemplated maintaining the SUMP reservoir at 70% to accommodate unexpected surges, but the level of protection possible if China supplies no advance warning remains unclear. This uncertainty is a thorn in the side of the government’s push against more legitimate resistance by Adi community members and civil rights groups. The need for the project does not excuse the state from following all the relevant laws and protections. The state cannot protect the nation’s needs by antagonising the nation’s people.

articles.title: Dwindling support: On the U.S. and the Cuban embargo
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Nearly every year since 1992, the United Nations General Assembly has passed a resolution calling on the U.S. to end its decades-old economic embargo on Cuba . As a result, the outcome at the UNGA resolution titled the ‘Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba’ passed on October 28, was expected. Surprisingly, the support for the resolution this year was dramatically lower than previous years. For the preceding decade, more than 180 countries of the 193-member UNGA had expressed their support for ending the embargo, but the numbers dropped to 165 in favour in 2025; this year’s tally dropped sharply lower, with 130 in favour, 25 abstaining and 17 countries voting against the resolution. The trend clearly points to efforts by the Trump administration to use its pressure on countries to change their votes, and many appear to have succumbed to those threats. Among those were several Latin American countries that have more recently grown closer to the U.S., particularly after the operation in Venezuela in January 2026 , where U.S. marines abducted President Maduro and brought him to the U.S. for a trial. Countries in the region such as Costa Rica, Ecuador, Argentina, and Colombia that have downgraded ties with Havana, switched votes on the resolution. In addition, U.S. diplomats argued that Havana-Moscow ties emboldened Russia’s war in Ukraine , which led to several western countries switching their vote. Diplomats from Ukraine and Poland, for example, referred to Cuba’s ties with Russia while explaining their vote, and Germany and Italy switched for the first time in many years to abstaining on the resolution. While it is clear that the bulk of the Group of 77 and non-aligned states including India maintained their support on the resolution for Cuba, the vote by the others demonstrates a disquieting turn.

Amidst these turns, New Delhi must be credited for standing firm on the issue , opposing the embargo, and calling for “dialogue and diplomacy” in its statement. The vote came a month after the BRICS New Delhi declaration expressed “deep concern” over the tightening of unilateral blockade measures on Cuba, and the “worrying humanitarian impact” on the Cuban people. It is important that India continue to stand up to such unilateral measures and amplify the voice of smaller countries, particularly those in the Global South.

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

articles.title: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s exasperation, during the Supreme Court’s hearing on October 29 on the “digital arrest” scams, that people still fall for such scams despite abundant warnings and orders from the Court is understandable. About ₹800 crore has been lost to these scams this year even after recoveries, a hefty sum from the savings of individual victims. But this is not merely about gullibility. Scammers posing as CBI or police officers succeed because their victims, older citizens in particular, defer to or fear law enforcement. When Indian police are widely seen as high-handed towards ordinary citizens and as serving only the powerful, the threat of an “arrest” over a video call cannot be that implausible for many. That said, the Court’s pressing of the Reserve Bank of India to finalise its KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, which require banks to flag suspected mule accounts and put temporary debit holds on them, is welcome. CBI investigations have shown that mule accounts are central to scammers laundering their proceeds after duping victims and that bank staff have, in some cases, helped open them. With the availability of complete transaction histories and AI tools, banks can now spot anomalous transactions faster. The Attorney-General’s assurance that the directions will be in force by December 31 is also welcome. The Court’s insistence that banks compensate victims addresses an issue with the RBI’s zero-liability provisions. Its 2017 circular covers only unauthorised transactions, leaving victims who were coerced into making transfers without any recourse.

Yet, full compensation for the victims whenever banks are found wanting in due diligence must be implemented with care as this might force banks to flag far more than the actual mule accounts. Already the RBI directions cast a wide net. Any transaction of ₹1,000 or more that is ‘unusual’ for an account holder’s declared profile, or linked to a reported account, can be held for up to 60 days, and longer if directed by the police. In cases where small traders and Jan Dhan account holders have unknowingly received transfers from mule accounts, freezing their accounts for two months or more is a disproportionate penalty. Also, the Court’s suggestion that unusual transactions must be automatically reported to the police and physically verified raises privacy concerns. These measures must ensure that genuine account holders are not penalised for bank failures. Many of these scams are run from compounds using trafficked Indians in conflict-ridden parts of Myanmar and in Cambodia and Laos where they have thrived due to some degree of official patronage. India must use its clout to pressure these regimes.

That said, the Court’s pressing of the Reserve Bank of India to finalise its KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, which require banks to flag suspected mule accounts and put temporary debit holds on them, is welcome. CBI investigations have shown that mule accounts are central to scammers laundering their proceeds after duping victims and that bank staff have, in some cases, helped open them. With the availability of complete transaction histories and AI tools, banks can now spot anomalous transactions faster. The Attorney-General’s assurance that the directions will be in force by December 31 is also welcome. The Court’s insistence that banks compensate victims addresses an issue with the RBI’s zero-liability provisions. Its 2017 circular covers only unauthorised transactions, leaving victims who were coerced into making transfers without any recourse.
• Yet, full compensation for the victims whenever banks are found wanting in due diligence must be implemented with care as this might force banks to flag far more than the actual mule accounts. Already the RBI directions cast a wide net. Any transaction of ₹1,000 or more that is ‘unusual’ for an account holder’s declared profile, or linked to a reported account, can be held for up to 60 days, and longer if directed by the police. In cases where small traders and Jan Dhan account holders have unknowingly received transfers from mule accounts, freezing their accounts for two months or more is a disproportionate penalty. Also, the Court’s suggestion that unusual transactions must be automatically reported to the police and physically verified raises privacy concerns. These measures must ensure that genuine account holders are not penalised for bank failures. Many of these scams are run from compounds using trafficked Indians in conflict-ridden parts of Myanmar and in Cambodia and Laos where they have thrived due to some degree of official patronage. India must use its clout to pressure these regimes.

articles.title: Suboptimal outcomes: On social security boards for unorganised, gig, platform workers
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: One year after the implementation of the Code on Social Security , the Union Labour Ministry has constituted the National Social Security Boards for Unorganised Workers and Gig and Platform Workers. The constitution of the boards, though delayed, is a welcome step. However, the highly centralised nature of this mechanism may hinder its optimal outcomes. By design, the Union Government controls both the Boards: they will be chaired by Union Minister for Labour Mansukh Mandaviya. The Board for Unorganised Sector Workers will have 40 members, nominated by the Union Government. They include seven members representing unorganised sector workers and seven members representing employers of the unorganised sector. Similarly, the Board for the welfare of gig and platform workers will have 22 members with five representatives each from the aggregators and the workers. But they have no significant representation of Central Trade Unions from the Opposition side or from the State Governments ruled by the Opposition. Labour is in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and both the States and the Union must work together to improve the living standards of workers.

The International Labour Organization defines social security as the ‘protection that a society provides to individuals and households to ensure access to health care and to guarantee income security, particularly in cases of old age, unemployment, sickness, invalidity, work injury, maternity or loss of a breadwinner’. The Union Government claims that the country’s social security coverage has increased from 19% in 2015 to 64.3% in 2025, which is around 94 crore citizens. However, it is apparent that the unorganised and gig and platform workers, who make up more than 92% of the country’s total workforce, are far from enjoying any social security under this definition. Almost two decades ago, the National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector, headed by economist Arjun Sengupta, recommended a slew of measures to improve the social security of workers in the informal sector. The issues raised by the panel still remain unaddressed. A report prepared by Justice V. Gopala Gowda for the Keralam Government in March this year flagged certain anti-federal and anti-worker characteristics in the Social Security Code and suggested amendments. The Union Government should take the trade unions and the State Governments on board while creating new systems and mechanisms to address the social security concerns of the vast majority of workers.

articles.title: Sanction 2,000 Indiramma houses in a week: Telangana Housing MD
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telangana Housing Department officials were directed to complete the sanctioning process of 2,000 Indiramma houses per Assembly constituency, under the second phase of the scheme, in a week’s time. First priority would be given to people living in huts.

With the success of the first phase of the housing project, people are eagerly waiting for the second phase, said the Corporation’s Managing Director V.P. Gautham. Selection process, remedies to delays in clearing bills for the beneficiaries, awareness of government facilitated cement bags and other aspects were discussed at a meeting with district project directors and deputy engineers, in Hyderabad on Monday (November 2, 2026).
Around 3.3 lakh houses were sanctioned under the first phase, and construction of around 2 lakh of them has been completed.

Mr. Gautham said that the State government issued guidelines for selection of beneficiaries who live in huts, which have to be adhered to. The officials were directed to allocate houses in coordination with public representatives and district in-charge ministers.

Awareness has to be created among people about the facility created by the government for the beneficiaries to buy cement at lower prices. The project directors were asked to inform people of the option to self-upload photos (of the houses) online to avoid delays in getting bills cleared.

articles.title: Anbumani opposes proposed ₹5 hike in Aavin milk prices
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss has urged the Tamil Nadu government to reject Aavin’s reported proposal to increase milk prices by ₹5 per litre, stating that it would place an additional burden on poor and middle-class families.

In a statement, he said the proposed hike followed a recent ₹6 per litre increase in the procurement price of milk supplied to Aavin, which was expected to widen the cooperative’s losses. Acknowledging that Aavin incurred a loss of ₹89.80 crore in 2025-26, he said increasing retail prices was not the only way to address its financial difficulties.

Pointing out that Aavin milk was considerably cheaper than products sold by private dairies, he said a ₹5 increase would amount to a hike of up to 12.5%. He called for addressing administrative inefficiencies and corruption in Aavin’s management and providing government subsidies to compensate for losses incurred in supplying milk at affordable prices.

articles.title: Over 2,100 potholes yet to be repaired in Chennai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) has identified 2,128 potholes and damaged road patches awaiting repair, as of Sunday. Street-wise identification is still under way, its latest status report said.

GCC Commissioner G.S. Sameeran on Monday flagged off 12 vehicles at the Ripon Buildings to repair potholes. The move follows Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s instruction to repair potholes using concrete and cold-mix materials as part of monsoon preparedness, a press release said.
Earlier, the GCC identified 8,160 potholes and damaged patches across 2,946 roads as on October 30. It completed repairs at 6,808 locations on interior and bus route roads by October 31.

GCC Commissioner G.S. Sameeran flagged off 12 vehicles from the Ripon Buildings complex to repair potholes caused by the Northeast monsoon using cold-mix material on November 2. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Tiruvottiyur zone has the highest number of pending repairs at 275, followed by Teynampet Zone at 273 and Tondiarpet Zone at 254. The report said Sholinganallur Zone had potholes at 168 locations, while Valasaravakkam Zone had the lowest number of locations with potholes, at 12.
The GCC has allocated ₹21.80 crore for pothole and patch repairs, including ₹12.55 crore for interior roads and ₹9.25 crore for bus route roads.

As on October 31, the GCC received 4,400 bags of cold-mix material and used 2,101. The remaining 2,299 bags were available for use. Repairs using the material covered 1,111 patches over 2,946.16 sq. m. The GCC has proposed procuring another 13,000 bags, weighing 325 tonnes.

articles.title: Clean energy investments helped India soften West Asia crisis impact: PM Modi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The impact of the West Asia crisis on India would have been more severe than the rest of the world had the country not made investments in renewable energy over the last decade, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said at the inauguration of the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (2026) in New Delhi Monday (November 2, 2026).

“Had India not made the investments it did in clean energy and building the requisite mechanisms [and infrastructure], the impact of the crisis would have been far more severe than in the rest of the world,” Mr. Modi said in his address. He also said that India’s economy continued to grow despite the crisis.
The Prime Minister put forth that the West Asia crisis exemplified how energy security was directly tied to economic security, adding that the future of energy security rested in clean energy.
He warned that excess dependence on fossil fuels could risk increased exposure to global disruptions.
Mr. Modi also said that India’s renewable energy sector would have investment opportunities of about $220 billion by the end of the decade.

In his pitch to potential investors, Mr. Modi held that it would be difficult to find the scale, scope and demand that India has in any other part of the world, alongside political and policy stability.
Mr. Modi emphasised that the next phase of solar revolution would rest on innovation.
He pointed to opportunities in the realm of indigenous manufacturing of essential hardware and battery storage systems, as well as in enhancing storage capacities.

Explaining his vision, the Prime Minister said, “We must carve out a dynamic where the country’s middle class has the option of an electric vehicle, and where they would be able to charge their scooty, bike, or car with solar-based energy. This would help save them a lot of money.”
He said the country would also require solutions that would help spur solar adoption in the dairy sector, animal husbandry, and farming.
Mr. Modi observed that India’s solar module manufacturing has grown from 2 gigawatts (GW) to 200 GW in a decade with the capacity to manufacture solar cells having grown to about 40 GW.
“Now we are working on enhancing [indigenous] manufacturing of other components as well,” he said.

articles.title: Man escaped from Coimbatore District Police custody arrested
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A 25-year-old man from Bhavani in Erode district, who escaped from the custody of police personnel escorting him to the Coimbatore Central Prison for judicial remand on October 31, was arrested on Monday (November 2).

Director-General of Police and Head of Police Force Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal confirmed the arrest to The Hindu . Sources said a special team of the police arrested Raghavan, reportedly from his native, on Monday evening. He was later brought to a location within the jurisdiction of the Coimbatore District (Rural) Police for questioning.

Raghavan, according to the police, has multiple cases against him in Erode and in Karnataka. He escaped first from the custody of the Karnataka police at a place within the jurisdiction of the Annur police in Coimbatore district on June 19, 2026, when they were bringing him back to Coimbatore after custodial interrogation in a case.

Since the escape happened within their jurisdiction, the Annur police had launched searches for Raghavan and arrested him on October 30. He escaped again from police custody, while being escorted to the Coimbatore Central Prison around 12.40 a.m. on October 31.
The Race Course police had registered a case in connection with the second escape and joint teams from Coimbatore city and rural were on the lookout for Raghavan , until his arrest on Monday.

articles.title: Air quality of Delhi slips to ‘very poor’ for first time this winter, Stage 2 of GRAP invoked
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: As the air quality of the national capital deteriorated to the 'very poor' category for the first time this winter season, the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and adjoining areas (CAQM) on Monday (November 2, 2026) announced Stage 2 of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP).

The air quality is likely to be in the 'very poor' category for the next three days, as per the Central government’s Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi. The last time Delhi’s air quality was in the 'very poor' category was on February 11 this year.

Stage 2 of the GRAP mandates NCR State governments to enhance vehicle parking fees to discourage use of private vehicles. The GNCTD (Delhi government) and NCR State governments also have to “stagger timings for public offices and municipal bodies in the National Capital Territory of Delhi and the districts of Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad and Gautam Buddha Nagar”.

Considering the restrictions on vehicles, the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has decided to run additional trips on weekdays. While the DMRC was running 20 trips since October 28, when the GRAP-1 was enforced, 20 more trips will be run now. “This is to encourage people to use public transport rather than their private vehicles and help mitigate pollution,” said a senior Metro official.
Other directions to State governments include implementing existing measures to control air pollution, such as mechanical sweeping of roads or sprinkling water on roads, among others

The GRAP is a set of short-term emergency measures to reduce air pollution and is divided into four stages. The CAQM announces the different stages depending on the level of pollution recorded or forecast for the near future.

The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi stood at 324 (very poor) at 4 p.m. on November 2, 2026, up from 261 (poor) a day earlier, as per the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)’s daily bulletin, which is treated as the day’s AQI. A higher AQI indicates worsening air quality.
‘Very poor' levels of air pollution could lead to “respiratory illness on prolonged exposure”, as per the CPCB. On February 11, 2026, the AQI was 305 (very poor).

Every winter, air pollution spikes in the Delhi-NCR and many parts of the larger Indo-Gangetic Plains, mainly due to meteorological factors such as lower wind speeds and a drop in temperature. Pollution from stubble burning during October and November and bursting of firecrackers during the festive season also add to existing pollution from vehicles and dust, worsening the air quality.

articles.title: Congress seeks JPC probe into IDBI Bank sale, alleges valuation irregularities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Congress on Monday (November 2, 2026) demanded an immediate halt to the proposed sale of IDBI Bank to Canada’s Fairfax Financial Holdings and a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) probe into the transaction, alleging that the government had manipulated the bank’s valuation.
The party alleged that the foreign buyer would use the bank’s own funds to finance the acquisition.

Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh separately described the transaction as a “major scam” by the Narendra Modi government and demanded that both valuation reports be made public.
Addressing a press conference, senior Congress leader Shaktisinh Gohil alleged that the disinvestment process was riddled with irregularities and lacked transparency.

Citing a conversation between an analyst and Fairfax Chairman Prem Watsa and President Peter Clarke, Mr. Gohil claimed that the company had indicated that the payment would be made in instalments, with the initial investment followed by the use of IDBI Bank’s resources to meet the remaining acquisition cost.
“Prem Watsa is a very close to Modi ji and had showered praise on him during the 2017 Vibrant Gujarat Summit,” the Congress leader said.

Mr. Gohil questioned the rationale of selling a profitable Indian bank to a foreign company using its own funds. He said IDBI Bank had earned a cumulative profit of ₹30,105 crore between 2021 and 2026 and had non-performing assets of only about 2%.
Its profit per employee stood at ₹49.8 lakh, making it one of the leading banks on this measure, he said. “Why is a bank that is delivering such high profits being sold?” he asked.

The Congress leader also questioned the revision of the bank’s valuation from ₹94.42 to ₹75 a share after the bids had been opened. He said the government had initially fixed the valuation at ₹94.42 a share before inviting bids, but subsequently revised it downwards.
The government was now claiming to have secured a good deal by selling the bank at ₹81 a share, he said, demanding disclosure of both valuation reports and the identity of the second bidder.

Mr. Gohil invoked an assurance given by the then Finance Minister Jaswant Singh in Parliament in August 2003 that the government’s stake in IDBI Bank would not be reduced below 51%. A Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance had also favoured retaining the government’s majority stake, he said.

He further questioned the regulatory concessions extended to Fairfax, including the two-year window reportedly allowed to reduce its control in another Indian bank, and sought details of the source of funds for the acquisition.

articles.title: Capex push to continue, but fiscal prudence non-negotiable: FM
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Union Finance and Corporate Affairs Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Monday reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to sustaining capital expenditure (capex) to support economic growth, while stressing that fiscal prudence would remain non-negotiable.

“Capex is a very important component of our growth strategy. Because till such time the private sector will be able to expand capacity or make capital investment, it is important for the Government to push through with capital investment,” she said at an event organised by HSBC India in Mumbai.
Pointing to the returns from public investment over the past four to five years, she said the multiplier effects had strengthened the Government’s confidence in continuing the spending push.

“We find that in the last 4 to 5 years, we have got very good success. The multipliers actually work and it gives us confidence that the Government is not going to sit back and watch whether growth is growing without doing much,” she said.

The Government would be willing to extend capex support to ensure that the growth momentum was not disrupted. “We will continue doing that because India’s growth momentum should not be lost at all,” she said.
However, Ms. Sitharaman made it clear that higher public spending would have to be balanced against fiscal constraints.
“We need to be fiscally prudent,” she said, adding that while some advocated spending without worrying about sovereign credit ratings, responsible expenditure was essential.
“I agree we need to spend but it has to be done responsibly and fiscal prudence will be our top priority,” she emphasised.
“We have to be prudent and we have to be creative based on which we can encourage growth and stability,” she added.
The Finance Minister also called for greater confidence in India’s economic prospects, urging businesses and experts to move beyond pessimism and sector-specific concerns.

“India must to talk with optimism and there needs to be reduction in cynicism,” she said, questioning why experts who considered their own sectors healthy remained apprehensive about the broader economy.
“If your sector doing fine, others sectors in India must be similarly fine. So can the narrate and language change?” she asked.

articles.title: No-cost EMI: a loan that is portrayed as free
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Every festive season, the same board greets you at the electronics shop: “No-cost EMI”. TVs, washing machines and appliances are available at no-cost EMI. A ₹60,000 phone, 6 easy instalments of ₹10,000, no interest. It feels as if the shopkeeper has done you a favour. He has not. Nobody lends money for free and nobody sells at a loss. Someone pays. Lets see who.

A bank or finance firm funds the purchase and charges interest. The shop agrees to bear interest but it will recover it in one of two ways. Either the price quoted to you is higher, or you lose the discount a cash buyer would have got Take the same phone. A cash buyer gets it for ₹57,000. The EMI buyer pays ₹60,000. The ₹3,000 gap is the interest.
